chunks: ‘Alī ibn Zayd ibn ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī narrated to me, saying:

I had a horse, and I was impressed with it, mentioning it often in gatherings. One day I entered upon Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, and he said to me, “What happened to your horse?” I said, “It is with me, and here it is at your door; I dismounted from it.” He said to me, “Exchange it before evening, if you can find a buyer, and do not delay that.” Then someone entered upon us, and the conversation was cut off.

So I rose up thinking and went to my home, and informed my brother of the matter. He said, “I do not know what to say about this.” I was reluctant concerning it and withheld it from people by selling it, and we entered the evening. Then the groom came to us after we had performed the night salat (prayer), and he said, “O my master, your horse has died.” So I became grieved and knew that this was what he had meant by those words.

He said: Then I entered upon Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام after some days, while saying to myself, “Would that he replace for me an animal, since I had been grieved by his words.” So when I sat, he said, “Yes, we shall replace an animal for you. O boy, give him my dark brown barḏawn. This is better than your horse, more easy to ride, and longer-lived.”

key_terms.السَّائِسُ: the groom or keeper of the horse
key_terms.الْكُمَيْتَ: dark brown or reddish-brown in color
key_terms.الْمَسَاءِ: the evening, before which the exchange was advised
key_terms.اِسْتَبْدِلْ: replace or exchange it for another
key_terms.بِرْذَوْنِيَ: my barḏawn, a strong riding beast or steed
key_terms.فَرَسٌ: a horse owned by the narrator
key_terms.نَفَقَ: died, referring to the horse’s death

ai.seo_question: How does this narration show the foreknowledge and generosity of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام informed the narrator, through a brief instruction, of the impending loss of his horse before it occurred. After the horse died that same evening, the narrator later returned, and the Imam عليه السلام replaced it with a better mount, demonstrating his foreknowledge and generosity.

en.hubeali:
Is’haq said, 
‘Ali Bin Zayd son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> narrated to me saying,

‘There was a horse for me, and I was fascinated by it and would frequently mention it in the gatherings. So I went over to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) one day, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘What happened to your horse?’ So I said, ‘It is with me, and it is that which is at your<sup>asws</sup> door, and I descended from it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Change it before the evening if you are able upon (finding a) buyer, and do not delay that’; and a comer entered and the speech was cut off.

So I stood up worried and I went to my house and I informed my brother of the news. So he said, ‘I do not know what I should be saying regarding this’. And I hesitated with it and I was unwilling upon the people with selling it, and evening came. So there came to us a (horse) groomer came over and we prayed the evening Salat, and he said, ‘O my master! Your horse died’. So I was gloomy and knew that this is what heasws had meant with that word.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then I went over to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> after a few days, and I was saying within myself, ‘If only he<sup>asws</sup> would replace the animal upon me when I was gloomy due to his<sup>asws</sup> words’. So when I was seated, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, we<sup>asws</sup> will replace the animal upon you. O boy! Give him my<sup>asws</sup> dark brown horse. This one is better than your horse, and more rideable, and of a longer life-span’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ishaq has said that narrated to him ’Isma‘il ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Ali ibn ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abbass ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib who has said the following.

“Once I sat on the side of the road waiting for abu Muhammad (a.s.) to pass by so that I can present before him my complain against a need. When he was passing by I presented my complain before him and swore that I did not have even a Dirham, nothing for lunch or dinner.”

The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) said, “You falsely swore by Allah. You have buried two hundred Dinars. These my words are not to deny you any grants. Young man, give him whatever is with you. His servant, give me one hundred Dinars. He then turned to me and said, “You will be deprived of it in your worst days.” He meant those Dinars that I had buried for a difficult day. What he said was true. I had buried two hundred Dinars thinking that they would only be used in a very difficult day. When I faced such a difficult day and all the ways to find a living was closed I went to take out the two hundred Dinars but soon I found that there was not even a single Dinar. In fact, my son had learned about where the Dinars were buried and he had taken them and had ran away. I could not benefit from any of those Dinars.”
